newsitem.title: UK: Clocks back one hour for British wintertime.
newsitem.headline: Clocks back one hour for British wintertime.

text.p: Britons on Sunday put their clocks back one hour to be in line with Greenwich Mean Time for the winter.
But insurance companies warned that the first few days of darker evenings could mean more road accidents.

Churchill Insurance said 1995 figures showed accidents rose by 10 percent in the week after the clock change compared with the week before. "Drivers must take much more care and caution in the coming months," a spokesman said.

The 15-nation European Union puts its clocks forward by an hour in summer under a policy aimed at saving energy and creating long summer evenings. Clocks in the EU went back an hour to winter time on Saturday.

But as EU members prepare to discuss the summer time regime which will apply from 1998, France has signalled it wants a break with the EU system which was originally agreed to create stability after the oil crisis.

A new French parliamentary report last week favoured setting a fixed time, setting its time at GMT plus one hour -- winter time in most countries -- and thus abandoning the twice yearly change of clocks.
Official French reports argue that energy savings are minimal in summer time and that farmers, truck drivers and children getting up early to go to school would benefit from lighter mornings.
